Internal helper: a call forwarded through a wrapper's ..., as typed

Source: R/plot.R
dot-jst_forwarded_args.Rd

.wrap <- function(...) jplot(...): inside jplot()'s generic, match.call() gives every argument the wrapper forwarded as ..1, ..2, names that point at the wrapper's promises. Until Session 369 (Fix Slate 16) the generic passed those names on, so jplot.default read them in its own terms: .wrap(data = h, Scor) said "the ..1 data frame", .wrap(Score) under a juse() default stopped on a variable named "..1", and .wrap(data = h, Score) with a separate Score in the workspace stopped on rlang's error, the generic having forced the promise. Each ..N is replaced here by the expression it forwards, read from the argument's quosure, which carries the environment the expression was typed in.

Usage

.jst_forwarded_args(mc, q_x, q_which, q_dots, caller_env)

Arguments

mc

The generic's match.call(expand.dots = TRUE).

q_x, q_which

The quosures of x and which, or NULL where the call does not give them.

q_dots

The dots' quosures, rlang::enquos(...).

caller_env

The environment the call was made from.

Value

A list: names, the arguments' names ("" where unnamed); typed, the arguments with each ..N replaced by the expression it forwards (for messages); args and env, what to evaluate and where; forwarded, whether any argument was forwarded; mixed, whether the arguments came from more than one environment.

Details

The direct call has no ..N and comes back unchanged, to be evaluated where it was made. A forwarded call is evaluated where the forwarded expressions were typed, as the direct call would be – but only when every argument that needs an environment shares that one. A wrapper that passes an object of its own beside the forwarded ones (function(dat, ...) jplot(data = dat, ...)) mixes two, and its arguments keep their ..N (mixed); the generic then passes a forced x as its quosure.

The quosures are taken in the generic's own frame, before anything forces an argument, and matched here to the call's arguments: x and which by name, the rest in order to the dots'. When the counts disagree, none is used and the call comes back unchanged.
